inspectedNativeSource.method: Read-only background inspection: linked intended collection into isolated evaluable scene; applied original recorded native cohorts with original helper and S 0 / E 90 / N 180 / W -90. Never saved source project.
inspectedNativeSource.nativeAtlases: All 16 production chef-dalia atlases, each 2304x1280,6 columns x 2 rows, 12 registered 384x640 cells. Exact source atlas rects and source/frame SHA256 in source-frame-manifest.json.
inspectedNativeSource.snapshotParity: inputs/original.png has identical RGBA pixels to production idle-S atlas cell 0.
inspectedNativeSource.visualInspection: All 192 source cells inspected through16 logical 192x320 gray-background sheets. Representative idle S/N,work E,hold S,load W also inspected at native 384x640 and on light/gray/dark at logical size. Raw original and target inspected directly; appearance-only normalization derivative expressly not registration evidence.
inspectedNativeSource.limits: This initial review is not a candidate verdict. Saved source pixel samples and evaluated transforms were inspected; actual12 fps motion playback and full all-mesh stable-topology/camera/socket audit remain mandatory candidate evidence. No exact measurements are inferred from the target.

originalVisibleAssessment.observation: A readable chunky chef with chocolate fringe and full back curls, broad face, very compressed coat/apron/feet. The cap reads as a blank white rectangular block from every direction; repeated equal-sized curls look stacked, and cuff/palm transitions are angular. Those weak forms and original part counts are open to improvement.

Ivory coat/cap, dark brown skin and chocolate hair, teal apron, bright red tie and very dark shoes form a useful identity palette. The white cap dominates and loses its surface shape; the small face and tie remain readable at logical size. The target is warmer and more luminous but should not bleach the skin, turn teal blue, or change the red tie.

Original hat has a nearly white flat interior with little form rolloff; original face and apron have broad flat surfaces and abrupt darker facets. Back curls are readable but repetitive and dark between lobes. Broad warm shading and restrained highlights should reveal the native volumes in every facing without a fixed horizontal key or ground shadow.

Original apron bib/skirt and coat collar carry only simple geometric cues; pocket is a small teal bar. Target collar/cuffs, apron band and pocket, tie knot, rounded shoes and curl highlights make the craft and garment layers more legible. Readable purpose matters more than reproducing every small seam or button.

Source silhouettes are complete and planted, but the bright cap is a large dead area. In work, sleeves bend into angular chunky forearms. The source held salmon appears high near the face, is visually detached from the lower inactive hand, and is hidden from N by the character; these are actual source composition caveats, not evidence of a new native 3D dish or a missing belt-release animation.

usefulOutcomes: Softer full head/limb forms with clean rounded transitions and a friendly face.
An ivory short chef hat with a readable band/crown and gentle fabric-like folds kept inside the functional source envelope.
Chocolate curls with larger intentional grouping and warm restrained highlights.
A constructed ivory coat and teal apron with readable collar/cuffs, bib/waist/pocket hierarchy; red necktie remains distinct.
Warm broad form shading, soft contact separation and appealing material contrast at logical use size.
referenceCaveats: Target canvas 971x1619, enlarged silhouette and root placement are not registered capture evidence; do not fit native frames to them.
Target skin appears orange and lighter than Dalia identity; warm dark brown skin must remain.
Target tall puffy toque is not a license to increase nominal height or replace the short ivory cap identity. A compact softened construction is acceptable.
Target bright rim/halo and its ragged alpha edge must not be copied.
Single front target supplies no exact unseen rear/side design. Coherence and useful native design are the standard there.
Family concept is style-only and has blue apron; Dalia apron remains teal.

actualSourceCaveats: Nominal authored functional height is 1.3750000298 world units, and idle/hold frame 0 top is 1.3749998808. Authored tilt/bob already raises evaluated tops: idle 1.3785212,work 1.3949051,hold 1.3785820,load 1.3948596. Do not falsely reject the existing motion for exceeding nominal rest height; preserve the original state/frame envelope allowance while keeping rest design within nominal height.

Source body remains within one cell, including work/load forward reach (~Y=-0.4943 canonical S). Source held image plane includes 0.6 cell camera-ray depth bias and reaches outside the body footprint geometrically; that plane is an explicitly declared 2D rendering attachment, not body geometry establishing a new occupied cell.

Feet are planted at world Z 0 to numerical noise throughout all sampled motions; source scale is 1.25 on ground root. Root origin is fixed. Preserve actual evaluated contacts rather than applying static metadata sockets directly as dynamic endpoints.

The held salmon is one packed RGBA image plane with camera-facing/yaw-cancellation behavior, visible in hold/load only. It must stay honestly labeled2D. No native 3D salmon claim; no full-character target billboard substitution.

Knife handle and blade are native 3D meshes visible during work only. Handle center matches evaluated right palm center within 1.3e-7 world units across S work frames. Preserve this actual attachment and its chopping behavior.

Source load extends arms/dish and returns to its start pose at frame 11 with dish still visible. The required load policy is nonloop even though endpoint pose returns. No separate named beltLoad object/recorded release trajectory exists in this source inventory; do not invent a belt placement/release requirement from the socket label.

The native source image plane is occluded in N. In S/E/W it is at face/chest height and is not a symmetric two-hand physical dish. Maintain the declared source attachment behavior and readable action; a candidate must show its source-relative comparison and clarify any purposeful correction rather than silently inventing new choreography.

Static catalog socket coordinates are rest metadata and differ from evaluated source native action controls. Candidate contacts must be checked against the isolated evaluated original, not read from a hidden/excluded source scene or guessed from an atlas.
Original camera record describes raw scale 4; runtime atlases use scale 2. A candidate must preserve logical 192x320/root 96,248/35 degree projection and384x640 capture, with honest scale 2 metadata.
Source visible selected-part loop closures for idle/work/hold match their frame 0 evaluated bounds exactly at native closing key 13; runtime atlases omit the closure frame.

attachments.knife: Visible native mesh handle and blade in work only; knife handle center coincides with evaluated right palm center within 1.3e-7 world units.
attachments.dish: Packed2D billboard in hold/load only;0.6 cell camera-ray bias; player-facing yaw cancellation; geometric planebounds are not character occupied footprint. Load extends then returns to first pose with dish visible.

rankedDesiredOutcomes.outcome: Replace the blank block-like hat and crude body/garment transitions with compact, purposeful soft native forms that read as Dalia in all four facings within her functional rest/motion envelope.
Use warm broad shading to show face, curls, ivory fabric and teal apron volumes; retain dark brown/chocolate/ivory/teal/red/dark identity and readable layered garments at logical size.
Keep all source motions, feet and actual hand/knife/2D dish attachment behavior coherent, complete and artifact-free through every registered native frame.
